title: VARADE: a Variational-based AutoRegressive model for Anomaly Detection on the Edge
problem: Existing deep learning-based anomaly detection solutions for Industry 4.0 are computationally demanding and require cloud architectures that suffer from latency and bandwidth constraints when processing massive data streams.
motivation: Real-time anomaly detection on edge devices is critical for Industry 4.0 to minimize latency and bandwidth overhead while maintaining detection accuracy.
method: VARADE implements a lightweight autoregressive framework using variational inference to enable efficient probabilistic anomaly detection on edge devices. The approach combines variational inference for efficient posterior approximation with an autoregressive architecture to model temporal dependencies in sequential data, enabling real-time execution on edge platforms.
key_novelty: A lightweight variational-inference-based autoregressive model optimized for real-time anomaly detection on resource-constrained edge devices.
contributions: Novel VARADE framework combining variational inference with autoregressive modeling for edge anomaly detection
Validation on real robotic arm in production line demonstrating practical applicability
Achieves optimal trade-off between anomaly detection accuracy, power consumption, and inference frequency
Evaluation across multiple edge platforms showing consistent efficiency gains
primary_theme: Efficient anomaly detection for edge devices
